title: API config design scratchpad (Alex)
content:
Goal:
- Capture a minimal, flexible API config schema that covers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Make configs composable (defaults + overlays per deployment/pool/model).
- Provide clear knobs for latency vs cost (batching, kv-cache, quantization profile).

Problem / constraints:
- Users want a single config surface for both hosted endpoints and private deployments; backend needs to resolve to platform-specific implementation details.
- Need safe defaults for ML teams that remove footguns (e.g., aggressive batching that breaks SLOs).
- Backwards compatibility: customers pin versions; changes must be additive.

Rough sketch of schema (YAML-style, informal):

endpoint: my-embedding-endpoint
model: sentence-embed-1.0
version: v1
route: production
policies:
  latency_slo_ms: 150
  cost_target: low    # enum: low | balanced | high (tradeoff)
  fallback_models: [sentence-embed-1.0-quant, sentence-embed-0.9]
serving:
  mode: pooled       # pooled | exclusive (dedicated) | serverless
  pool: gp-pool-8    # optional reference to Dedicated pool id
  concurrency: 8     # per-device concurrency hint
  autoscale:
    min: 1
    max: 10
    scale_policy: cpu_based
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_size: 64
  timeout_ms: 12     # target batching latency (ms)
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  prefix_cache: true
quantization_profile: q4_0
logging:
  level: info
  trace_sample_rate: 0.01

Notes on fields:
- mode/pool: we resolve this at runtime to either hosted (managed pool) or to customer's dedicated pool id. For private deployments, pool maps to local node group.
- latency_slo_ms: used by routing to decide whether to route to a lower-cost fallback. If request has urgency header, routing ignores cost.
- quantization_profile: a key knob; should accept explicit profile names plus an 'auto' option that the optimizer can recommend.

Example API request (shape):
POST /v1/endpoints/my-embedding-endpoint/config-apply
Payload:
{
  "version": "v1.2",
  "overrides": {
    "policies.cost_target": "balanced",
    "batching.timeout_ms": 8,
    "serving.mode": "exclusive",
    "kv_cache.prefix_cache": false
  }
}

Design decisions to validate:
- Allow dotted-path overrides (simpler UX) vs fully typed patch objects (safer).
- If dotted paths allowed, we need server-side validation and an audit trail.
- How to present effective config in console (merged view, show origin of each key).

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- alpha: internal-only, CLI + SDK apply, no console. Only hosts with feature-flag.
- beta: enable console UI (merged config view) and audit logs; open to select customers.
- GA: public docs, schema validation in SDKs, migration tools.

Operational hooks we need:
- config.validate endpoint (dry-run validate without applying runtime changes)
- config.preview endpoint (show merged config for a given endpoint + model + pool)
- config.apply (apply and record audit entry)

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Namespacing: should we allow free-form keys under 'platform' for provider-specific knobs? e.g., aws: { instance_type } vs platform.aws.instance_type.
- [ ] Compute budget field: how to express reserved GPU-hours vs ephemeral burst? Align with Dedicated pricing model.
- [ ] Migration story: if we change batching defaults, how do we notify customers or auto-toggle?
- [ ] Add explicit 'safety'/rate-limit quota keys to help protect models from prompt injection/hammering.

Links / references:
- Confluence config docs (linked above) contains current proposal and validation matrix.
- ENG ticket JIRA-ENG-3245 tracks validation + audit log work.
- Relevant PR: serving-runtime/pull/789 (kernel selection + config hook)

Sketch of console merged-config UI (text diagram):
[Dropdown: endpoint] -> [Merged config table]
Columns: key | effective value | origin (default / overlay name) | last_changed_by | last_changed_at
Rows: policies.latency_slo_ms | 150 | default | system | 2025-10-01
      batching.max_batch_size | 64  | overlay:squad-x  | Casey  | 2025-11-05

Quick notes to self for next session:
- Sync with product-hosted-api about UX for dotted overrides.
- Validate that existing SDKs can roundtrip dotted overrides through JSON (some languages marshaling issues).
- Add unit tests around preview merging with conflicting overlays (order of precedence).

Scratch ideas for future features:
- 'Workload profile' presets (low-latency, high-throughput, inference-batch-job) that set multiple knobs.
- Config diff view (compare two overlays or overlay vs default).

-- Alex 
(Notes: messy; will tidy before sending to product. keeping as quick capture of decisions + TODOs)
